title: LLM routing + KV-prefetch parking lot
content:
Context:
- Working through ideas for combining smart routing with KV-prefetch (prefix caching) to reduce tail latency + token cost for chat-heavy workloads.
- Many teams have asked for a way to bias routing to cached model instances (or warmed KV states) without sacrificing correctness. This doc is a parking-lot of user stories, heuristics, and experimental ideas.

Goal:
- Surface a set of practical experiments we can try in Dedicated/Hosted to measure latency and cost gains from routing->prefetch integration.
- Capture product/user needs and minimal API/telemetry changes required.

Problem statement:
- Cold KV cache leads to increased token generation latency for interactive chat.
- Global routing decisions today are mostly model/version/region/capacity driven, not cache-awareness.
- If we route naive requests to instances without KV, users see 100-300ms extra per response (depending on model seq length).
- Prefer warm instances for returning users / multi-turn flows but must avoid pathological routing (infinite loops, hot-spotting).

User personas / stories (rough):
- As a product engineer, I want my chat app to prefer instances that already have the user's session KV so that replies are faster and cheaper.
- As an infra engineer, I want routing heuristics to degrade gracefully when no warmed instance exists (fallback path).
- As a SRE/ops person, I want visibility into cache-hit routing vs default routing and ability to throttle cache-prefetching to control GPU/IO load.

Acceptance criteria for initial experiment:
- Per-request latency 5-15% lower p95 on synthetic multi-turn workloads (10-turn average) vs baseline.
- Token cost per session measured and show >=8% improvement for high prefix reuse patterns.
- No increase in error rate or request failures.
- New telemetry exposed: routed_to_warm_instance (boolean), kv-prefetch-invoked (boolean), prefetch-time-ms (numeric).

Ideas / heuristics to try (ranked):
1) Taint-based quick wins:
   - Keep lightweight metadata on instances: last_seen_session_ids (LRU n=1000), estimated_kv_warm_score.
   - On request, if session_id present and instance has session_id -> prefer that instance.
   - Fallback: heuristic score = (warm_score * 0.7) + (latency_score * 0.3) so we don't pick a slower instance just because it's warm.

2) Predictive prefetch (async):
   - After request completes, prefetch likely next prefixes for the session to a small set of warm instances (N=2).
   - Prefetch pipeline is rate-limited per-customer to avoid IO spikes.
   - Track prefetch success/failure and backoff aggressively on misses.

3) Cache-aware batching:
   - When batching requests, prefer grouping by warmed prefix to maximize KV reuse.
   - If batch contains mixed sessions, consider splitting micro-batches at cost of throughput. Experiment tradeoffs.

4) Graceful degradation policies:
   - If warm-instance load > threshold (cpu/gpu mem or queued requests), route to cold fallback models rather than overload warms.
   - Use short TTL for session->instance mappings (e.g., 5 minutes) to avoid stale routing.

5) Privacy/safety considerations:
   - Session metadata should be opaque ids only (no PII).
   - Option to disable cache-routing at tenant-level for regulatory customers.

Telemetry / instrumentation (minimal):
- RoutedToWarmInstance: true/false (per request)
- PrefetchInvoked: true/false
- PrefetchSuccess: true/false
- PrefetchTimeMs: stringified numeric
- WarmScoreAtRouting: numeric (binned)
- CacheHitAfterRouting: true/false (did subsequent requests reuse cached KV)

Metrics to collect for experiments:
- p50/p95/p99 latency (generation + end-to-end) per workload
- Token cost per session (billing proxy)
- Prefetch IO cost (#prefetches * size)
- Warm instance utilization and queuing depth
- Incorrect-route rate (e.g., session routed to instance without expected KV)

Operational knobs (expose in console):
- Aggressiveness slider: {conservative, balanced, aggressive} mapping to prefetch rate and routing bias.
- TTL for session->instance mapping
- Max concurrent prefetches per-customer
- Prefetch backoff policy (exponential with jitter)

Design options (pros/cons high-level):
- Centralized mapping store (single source of truth): easier to reason about but additional cross-region latency and potential SPOF.
- Distributed soft-state per-instance LRU: simpler, low-latency decisions but eventual consistency and more complex collision handling.
- Hybrid: central index for coarse routing + local per-instance fine-grained store for last-mile. Probably the best initial tradeoff.

Queues & scaling concerns:
- Prefetch can create IO bursts on cold KV loads and model weight caching. Must limit concurrency per-customer and global.
- Need circuit breaker if prefetch latency spikes; otherwise we risk slow requests while waiting for prefetch. Async prefetch preferred.

Experiment plan (MVP):
- Phase 0: instrumentation only. Add telemetry flags to baseline routing calls (2 weeks).
- Phase 1: soft-state per-instance LRU and routing bias (A/B test on 5% tenants) (3 weeks).
- Phase 2: predictive async prefetch (10% tenants, monitor IO & cost) (4 weeks).
- Phase 3: wider rollouts + console knobs, migration to hybrid index if needed (4-6 weeks).

Open questions / risks:
- How many session IDs do we realistically need to track per instance before benefits taper? (simulate with production traces)
- Are we hitting any platform limits (e.g., network egress when prefetching KV across zones)?
- Cost model: prefetching reduces generation tokens but increases IO/GPU ops—net cost unclear. Need experiments to measure end-to-end USD/session.
- Risk of hot-spotting a few instances for popular customers -> need fair-share/weighting.

Concrete next steps (TODOs):
- [ ] Get trace sample from telemetry team with session-id frequency distribution (ask Priya). (JIRA-7890)
- [ ] Add experimental telemetry fields to runtime + backend (Jordan -> PR branch).
- [ ] Prototype per-instance LRU store (in-memory) and simple routing bias function. Scope: no cross-region first. (Aisha)
- [ ] Mock workload that simulates multi-turn chat with varying reuse patterns (Noah).
- [ ] Cost estimate doc: rough USD per 1000 sessions for conservative/balanced/aggressive.

Notes to self:
- Keep initial changes feature-flagged behind tenant opt-in.
- Talk to console team about how to visualize warm vs cold routing (timeline per session).
- Remember to check Dedicated autoscaling behavior when warms are preferred—might need to enlarge warm pool size.

References / related notes:
- See users/llm-prefetch-kv-cache-scratchpad.json and users/llm-routing-prefetch-scratchpad-jamie-park.json for overlapping ideas.
- Related PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/412 (prefetch helper lib).

End parking-lot. Will turn a subset into a rough PRD after we have first telemetry runs.

-- Jordan
